title: Implications of Study on Excess Mortality During COVID-19 Pandemic
what_it_is: Implications of Study on Excess Mortality During COVID-19 Pandemic

sections.label: Excess mortality COVID-19 study
sections.summary: Asked whether excess mortality from COVID-19 will be studied further and what is done to identify preventable causes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health (a) whether there will be a continued, further and deeper study of excess mortality from the COVID-19 pandemic including the impact of COVID-19's long-term effects and how this may contribute to excess mortality; and (b) what is being done to identify potentially preventable causes of excess mortality.

sections.label: Excess deaths rate 2020-2022
sections.summary: Between January 2020 and June 2022, deaths rose 24.9 per 100,000 persons per year against 2019 baseline.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Between January 2020 and June 2022, there was an increase of 24.9 deaths per 100,000 persons per year, using the pre-COVID-19 year of 2019 as the baseline.

sections.label: Unvaccinated share of COVID-19 deaths
sections.summary: In first half of 2022, about 5% of eligible population were not fully vaccinated but contributed 28% of COVID-19 deaths.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: In the first half of 2022, about 5% of the eligible population are not fully vaccinated, but they contributed to 28% of COVID-19 deaths.

sections.label: COVID-19 death rates comparison
sections.summary: This group's observed COVID-19 death rate was about two in 1,000 versus 0.3 in 1,000 population-wide.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: For this group, the observed rate of COVID-19 deaths in these individuals was about two in 1,000, compared to 0.3 in 1,000 observed in the whole population.

sections.label: Drivers of excess deaths
sections.summary: Numbers not compiled, but literature and experience show vaccination status and age are the two main drivers of excess deaths.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Maybe that is something they can look into but, so far, we have not compiled those numbers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: But if we look at the literature and our own experience, the two main drivers of excess deaths have been, first, are you vaccinated?

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Second, your age, and that will continue to be the case.

sections.label: Booster rate and living with virus
sections.summary: Moving forward, booster rate matters and counting boosters should stop, moving to living with the virus like influenza.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Moving forward, it is more the booster rate and we should move to a stage where we stop counting the number of boosters, such as booster one, two, three and so on, but move to a concept where we really live with the virus closer to how we live with influenza.
